name: Sigiriya and Dambulla
tagline: A 200-metre rock fortress with a palace on its summit, ancient frescoes and a mirror wall, beside a cave temple painted with Buddhas.
highlight: Reaching the summit of Sigiriya Rock, with the ruined palace beneath your feet and the jungle spread to the horizon.
shortDescription: The 5th-century rock fortress of Sigiriya, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, with frescoes, water gardens and lion's paw gates, plus Pidurangala Rock and the cave temples of Dambulla.
metaDescription: A Sigiriya and Dambulla travel guide: climbing Sigiriya Rock, the frescoes and mirror wall, water gardens, Pidurangala sunrise, Dambulla Cave Temple, tickets, best time and a two-day plan.
nearestAirport: Colombo Bandaranaike (CMB), about 4–5 hours by road
knownFor: Lion Rock fortress, frescoes, cave temples
budget: US$60–120 per day, mid-range, plus high entry fees

image.alt: The huge rock of Sigiriya rising above the jungle

intro: Sigiriya, or Lion Rock, is a 200-metre granite column rising from the jungle plain in central Sri Lanka, and the site of one of Asia's most extraordinary ancient cities. In the 5th century CE, King Kashyapa, who had seized the throne by killing his father, built a palace on its flat summit and a garden city at its foot. After his defeat, the site became a Buddhist monastery, and was abandoned around the 14th century. It is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The climb takes about an hour, up staircases past the remains of the Lion Gate, where two huge stone paws survive, and the Mirror Wall, once so polished that the king could see himself in it. On the way, a sheltered gallery holds frescoes of celestial maidens, painted 1,500 years ago. At the summit, the ruins of the palace and a pool give views across the forests. The symmetrical water gardens at the foot are among the oldest surviving landscape gardens in Asia.

Nearby Pidurangala Rock offers a less crowded view of Sigiriya itself at sunrise, and Dambulla, 20 km away, has a cave temple with more than 150 Buddha statues and painted ceilings. Entry to Sigiriya is expensive for foreigners, and the site can be very hot and busy, so go early.

whyVisit.intro: Sigiriya is Sri Lanka's most spectacular ancient site.
